title: Chilaquiles Red Salsa

seo.title: Red Chilaquiles Recipe: Authentic Mexican Breakfast
seo.metaDescription: Learn how to make delicious Red Chilaquiles with our easy, authentic Mexican recipe. Perfect for breakfast or brunch, featuring crispy tortillas and rich red salsa.

seo.imageCaption: Savor the rich flavors of homemade Red Chilaquiles, a classic Mexican breakfast dish.

description: Chilaquiles Rojos are a quintessential Mexican breakfast, featuring crispy corn tortilla pieces bathed in a rich, spicy red salsa. This heartwarming dish offers a perfect blend of textures and bold flavors, making it an irresistible start to any day. Traditionally garnished with fresh cheese, crema, and onion, it's a true taste of authentic Mexico.

instructions.title: Prepare Salsa Base
instructions.text: Place the halved Roma tomatoes, serrano peppers, garlic cloves, and chopped white onion in a saucepan. Cover with water and bring to a boil. Cook for about 10-12 minutes, or until the tomatoes are soft and their skins begin to split.

instructions.title: Blend the Red Salsa
instructions.text: Drain the cooked vegetables, reserving about 1/4 cup of the cooking water. Transfer the cooked tomatoes, peppers, garlic, and onion to a blender. Add 1 cup of chicken broth and 1 teaspoon of salt. Blend until completely smooth. If the salsa is too thick, add a little of the reserved cooking water.

instructions.title: Fry the Tortilla Chips
instructions.text: Heat 3-4 cups of vegetable oil in a large skillet or Dutch oven over medium-high heat. Once hot, carefully add the quartered corn tortillas in batches, frying until golden brown and crispy, about 3-5 minutes per batch. Remove with a slotted spoon and place on paper towels to drain excess oil. Sprinkle with a pinch of salt.

instructions.title: Simmer the Red Salsa
instructions.text: In a separate medium saucepan, heat 1 tablespoon of vegetable oil over medium heat. Carefully pour the blended salsa into the hot oil. Bring the salsa to a gentle simmer, stirring occasionally, and cook for 10-15 minutes, allowing it to thicken slightly and deepen in flavor. Taste and adjust salt if needed.

instructions.title: Combine Tortillas and Salsa
instructions.text: Just before serving, add the fried tortilla chips directly into the simmering red salsa. Gently toss to coat all the chips. Cook for 1-2 minutes, just long enough for the chips to absorb some of the sauce without becoming completely soggy.

instructions.title: Serve and Garnish
instructions.text: Immediately transfer the chilaquiles to individual serving plates. Drizzle generously with crema Mexicana, sprinkle with crumbled queso fresco, thinly sliced red onion, and fresh chopped cilantro. Serve hot and enjoy this classic Mexican breakfast.

tips: For truly crispy tortillas that hold up, fry them until golden and slightly firm, not just soft. This prevents them from becoming too soggy too quickly.
Adjust the spice level by increasing or decreasing the number of serrano peppers. For a milder version, you can substitute serranos with jalapeños or even omit them.
Serve chilaquiles immediately after combining the chips and salsa to enjoy the best texture. They are best enjoyed hot and fresh, as the tortillas will continue to soften over time.
